description: Rooftop panels feeding a shared battery so the block keeps the lights on together. Surplus energy is gifted to households that need it most.
name: Neighbourhood Solar Microgrid

value_cards.because: Energy is not a commodity in this grid; it is a form of care. The point of community infrastructure is to make the floor higher, not the ceiling.
value_cards.care_about: Building grid capacity so that the households most vulnerable to outages — elderly, medical equipment, young children — are the last to go dark.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: Grid that distributes evenly regardless of need. Solar as a cost-saving measure that benefits those who can already afford panels.
value_cards.in_conflict: The household that would lose heat or refrigerated medication over average distribution.
looks_like: Prioritising battery allocation to highest-need households in a shortage
Designing the system so the most vulnerable are protected without having to ask
Publishing real-time generation and allocation data for all members
value_cards.never_do: Design the system in a way that benefits contributors more than the most vulnerable.
value_cards.title: Energy resilience as mutual aid

value_cards.because: We built this together. The surplus belongs to whoever needs it most, not to whoever has the biggest array.
value_cards.care_about: Routing any generation above collective needs to households experiencing hardship — not selling it back to the grid, giving it to neighbours.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: Treating surplus as a personal financial return. Exporting to the grid while a neighbour can't afford to heat their home.
value_cards.in_conflict: The neighbour in difficulty over our own credit balance.
looks_like: Establishing a "gift pool" for surplus rather than grid export by default
Reviewing allocation quarterly with the whole grid community
Making it easy to signal need without stigma
value_cards.never_do: Sell surplus while a member is rationing their own use.
value_cards.title: Surplus energy as a gift
